key_insight: Capping CsPbBr3 thin films with few-layer hBN greatly improves heat dissipation without changing the perovskite’s morphology or optical behavior.
engineering_relevance: This offers a transparent, thermally conductive interface strategy to reduce overheating in perovskite solar cells and other high-excitation optoelectronic devices.
method: Planar hot-pressed CsPbBr3 thin films were prepared as the perovskite base layer.
A large-scale semidry transfer method was used to integrate few-layer 2D hBN onto the films.
Microscopy, spectroscopy, and heat-diffusion simulations were used to assess compatibility and thermal performance.
evidence_signal: The hBN-capped heterostructure showed a thermal conductivity of about 3 W/(m·K), roughly 7× higher than bare CsPbBr3 films (0.45 W/(m·K)), and was less affected by laser-induced heating under high-power continuous-wave excitation.
watch_item: The approach must preserve perovskite integrity during transfer and scaling, since interface quality and process compatibility are critical for real-device implementation.
paper_title: Improved Heat Dissipation in CsPbBr${_3}$-hBN Heterostructures
